content.text: {"headline":"No action needed: hold the current plan. Service level is predicted at 87.9% for 12:30–19:45, above the 80% target, at no extra cost.","why":"Calls are above forecast on both queues (payments +16%, general +28%), and payments dropped as low as 17.8–30% in the busy intervals earlier. The cause is extra demand that no IT incident, marketing send or absence explains. Even so, the forecast for the disruption window (12:30–19:45) with no changes is 87.9% overall. That is payments 89.4% and general 86.2%, with 2.6% abandons and 86.9% for the rest of the day. Every option clears the 80% target, so the cheapest one that follows policy is to do nothing. No escalation is flagged.","trade_offs":["P1 (no-cost rebalance) is predicted to do slightly worse than no action: 86.1% service level and 3.4% abandons. Moving 2 agents from payments to general lowers payments to 87.9%.","P2 (deflection plus late cover) adds only 0.5 points (88.4%) for ₹1,116, and abandons are about the same at 2.8%.","P4 reaches 90.4% with 2.5% abandons for ₹2,196. It is the best middle option if you want more of a buffer.","P3 gives the strongest result: 91.5% service level, 2.0% abandons and general at 91.9%. It costs ₹6,840 for about 3.6 points more than no action."],"watch":"The cause of the surge is unknown, so it could grow. Watch general most closely, since it has the thinnest margin at 86.2%, and also check payments in the busy intervals. If service level heads toward 80% or demand keeps climbing above forecast, P4 is the ready fallback at ₹2,196."}
